In [[functional analysis]], the '''Birkhoff–Kellogg invariant-direction theorem''', named after [[George David Birkhoff|G. D. Birkhoff]] and [[Oliver Dimon Kellogg|O. D. Kellogg]],<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Birkhoff, G. D.|author2=Kellogg, O. D.|title=Invariant points in function space|journal=Trans. Amer. Math. Soc.|year=1922 |volume=23|pages=96–115|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/tran/1922-023-01/S0002-9947-1922-1501192-9/S0002-9947-1922-1501192-9.pdf|doi=10.1090/s0002-9947-1922-1501192-9|doi-access=free}}</ref> is a generalization of the [[Brouwer fixed-point theorem]]. The theorem<ref>{{cite book|author1=Granas, Andrzej|author2=Dugundji, James|authorlink2=James Dugundji|title=Fixed Point Theory|year=2003|location=New York|publisher=Springer-Verlag|pages=125–126|isbn=0-387-00173-5|url=https://books.google.com/books?isbn=0387001735}}</ref> states that:

Let ''U'' be a bounded open neighborhood of '''0''' in an infinite-dimensional normed linear space ''V'', and let ''F'':∂''U'' → ''V'' be a compact map satisfying ||''F''(''x'')|| ≥ α for some α > 0 for all ''x'' in ∂''U''. Then ''F'' has an invariant direction, ''i.e.'', there exist some ''x''<sub>o</sub> and some ''λ'' > 0 satisfying ''x''<sub>o</sub> = ''λF''(''x''<sub>o</sub>).

The Birkhoff–Kellogg theorem and its generalizations by [[Juliusz Schauder|Schauder]] and [[Jean Leray|Leray]] have applications to partial differential equations.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Morse, Marston|authorlink=Marston Morse|title=George David Birkhoff and his mathematical work, VI. MISCELLANEOUS WORKS, (a) Fixed points in function space, pages 385–386|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.|year=1946|volume=52|issue=5, Part 1|pages=357–391|mr=0016341|doi=10.1090/S0002-9904-1946-08553-5|doi-access=free}}</ref>
